summary: Lymecycline is a second-generation tetracycline antibiotic used mainly for moderate to severe acne and for tetracycline-sensitive infections. It is bacteriostatic, inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis at the 30S ribosomal subunit. It offers good oral absorption and once-daily dosing for acne. Like other tetracyclines it is contraindicated in pregnancy, breastfeeding, and young children because of effects on developing teeth and bones, and it causes photosensitivity. It is not FDA-approved but is widely used under EMA/UK (BNF/SmPC) labeling.
indications: Treatment of infections caused by tetracycline-susceptible organisms (e.g., respiratory, urinary, and some sexually transmitted infections) where appropriate

dosage.d: 408 mg (= 300 mg tetracycline base) once daily
dosage.n: Continue for at least 8 weeks; review response

dosage.d: As per adult dosing (avoid in younger children)

admin: Swallow capsules whole with a full glass of water
Take while sitting or standing and avoid lying down for a while afterwards to prevent oesophageal irritation
Can be taken with or without food (absorption less affected than older tetracyclines)
Separate from dairy, antacids, and iron/zinc/calcium products by 2-3 hours (chelation reduces absorption)
Complete the prescribed course for infections; acne requires several weeks for benefit
moa: Lymecycline is a tetracycline that reversibly binds to the 30S ribosomal subunit of susceptible bacteria, blocking the attachment of aminoacyl-tRNA to the messenger RNA-ribosome complex and thereby inhibiting bacterial protein synthesis. This bacteriostatic action, combined with anti-inflammatory effects, underlies its use in acne. It is a more soluble lysine-formaldehyde condensation product of tetracycline.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to lymecycline or other tetracyclines
monitor: Hepatic and renal function with prolonged use

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Tetracyclines cross the placenta and can cause permanent discoloration of the deciduous teeth, enamel hypoplasia, and inhibition of fetal bone growth; maternal hepatotoxicity has also been reported.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding. Tetracyclines are excreted in breast milk and may affect the infant's developing teeth and bones; theoretical risk of dental staining.
renal: Use with caution and generally avoid in significant renal impairment. Tetracyclines have an antianabolic effect that can raise blood urea and worsen pre-existing renal dysfunction.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment and avoid concomitant potentially hepatotoxic drugs, as high doses of tetracyclines have been associated with hepatotoxicity.

major: Oral retinoids (e.g., isotretinoin, acitretin) - risk of benign intracranial hypertension; avoid combination
Vitamin A in high doses - additive intracranial hypertension risk
moderate: Divalent/trivalent cations (calcium, magnesium, aluminium antacids, iron, zinc) - chelation reduces absorption; separate doses
Warfarin - tetracyclines may potentiate anticoagulant effect
Penicillins - bacteriostatic tetracyclines may antagonise bactericidal penicillins
Combined oral contraceptives - prudent additional contraceptive advice (historical caution)
minor: Antiepileptics inducing metabolism (may reduce tetracycline levels)
interactions.food: Dairy products reduce absorption via calcium chelation - separate intake; otherwise food has limited effect
interactions.alcohol: No major direct interaction; moderation advised, especially with hepatic concerns
interactions.diagnostics: May raise blood urea nitrogen; can cause false elevations in urinary catecholamine assays

monitoring: Clinical response of acne or infection
Hepatic and renal function during prolonged therapy
counsel: Take with a full glass of water and stay upright for a while to protect your gullet
Avoid taking it at the same time as milk, antacids, or iron/zinc supplements - leave a 2-3 hour gap
Use sun protection and avoid sunlamps - your skin may burn more easily
Do not use if you are or may become pregnant, or while breastfeeding
Acne improvement can take several weeks - keep taking it as prescribed
Report severe headache with visual changes, persistent diarrhoea, or yellowing of skin/eyes
pk: Absorbed rapidly; antibacterial effect within hours, acne benefit over weeks
Plasma peak roughly 1-3 hours after an oral dose
Elimination half-life approximately 10 hours, supporting once-daily acne dosing
Once-daily dosing maintains adequate levels for acne therapy
Store below 25 C; protect from light and moisture
pearls: NOTE: Lymecycline is NOT FDA-approved; this record follows EMA/UK SmPC and BNF labeling rather than US prescribing information
408 mg lymecycline is equivalent to 300 mg of tetracycline base
Better solubility and absorption than older tetracyclines, allowing once-daily acne dosing
Standard tetracycline cautions apply: avoid in pregnancy, lactation, and children <12 years
Avoid combining with oral retinoids due to intracranial hypertension risk
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember with a full glass of water. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed one and continue as normal - do not take a double dose.
overdose: Overdose may intensify gastrointestinal effects (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea) and, with very high doses, hepatic and renal toxicity. There is no specific antidote; treatment is supportive and symptomatic. Dialysis is not effective. Avoid taking with milk to limit absorption.
